claims.statement: For every nonempty ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star profile, every original leaf deletion polynomial A_v (A0 for the endpoint or Ai for a tip of branch i), and every natural k with 1<=k and 2k<=N+2, integer-zero-extended coefficients satisfy A_v[k+1] C[k-1]<=A_v[k] C[k], where C=GQ.
claims.scope: Guarded lower-half shifted C-to-each-deletion comparison on all such k; no actual eligibility premise. It would imply full strict selection at actual eligible p via C log-concavity and the accepted C[x+1]/C[x]<1, but that universal comparison is unproved. Profile and polynomial definitions: Ordinary tree formed from path 0-1-2 and m>=1 distinct centers at 0, each with r_i in {2,3,4} private tips. N=sum_i r_i, L=1+z, G=1+2z, B_r=L^r+z, H_i=product_(h!=i)B_(r_h), Q=product_i B_(r_i), C=GQ, A0=LQ+zL^N, Ai=G B_(r_i-1)H_i+zL^N. Coefficients are integer zero-extended. The comparison imposes only its stated k guard; it does not presume actual first-descent eligibility.
claims.reason: No guarded counterexample appeared in six targeted exact profiles, and the comparison has a rigorous conditional implication to all current-p strict selectors at actual eligible ranks. The universal guarded comparison remains unproved; the finite checks are bounded evidence only.

A strict descent of W at actual eligible p gives at least one selected branch and, with the reviewed branchwise 3/2 bound, pays MASS. It does not assert that every tip or the endpoint is selected. Profile and polynomial definitions: Ordinary tree formed from path 0-1-2 and m>=1 distinct centers at 0, each with r_i in {2,3,4} private tips. N=sum_i r_i, L=1+z, G=1+2z, B_r=L^r+z, H_i=product_(h!=i)B_(r_h), Q=product_i B_(r_i), C=GQ, A0=LQ+zL^N, Ai=G B_(r_i-1)H_i+zL^N. Coefficients are integer zero-extended. The comparison imposes only its stated k guard; it does not presume actual first-descent eligibility.
claims.reason: This is a distinct weaker structural obligation than the individual comparisons. It remains open; finite individual-profile checks do not prove the universal weighted inequality, and the exact original multiplicities must be retained.

claims.statement: For an ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star, assume C is positive and log-concave on its support, Delta_x C<0 at the actual least strict descent x of P, and A_v[k+1]C[k-1]<=A_v[k]C[k] on 1<=k with 2k<=N+2. At every actual eligible p satisfying x+2<=p, 3p<2alpha+1, and 2p<=alpha, if A_v[p]>0 then Delta_p A_v<0; hence the strict selector is evaluated as selected at that current p.
claims.scope: Conditional informal proof for each original endpoint or private-tip deletion polynomial A_v, with actual first strict descent x, all three eligibility guards, zero-extended coefficients, and strict current-p selector. Uses the lower-half shifted comparison at k=p, not a no-recovery assumption for P.
claims.reason: Log-concavity makes C[p]/C[p-1]<=C[x+1]/C[x]<1 since p>=x+2. Dividing the shifted comparison by positive C[p-1] gives A_v[p+1]<=A_v[p]C[p]/C[p-1]<A_v[p]. The deletion coefficients are positive throughout this lower-half domain.

Coefficients: E[27]=1654284096099796392, E[28]=2450791253481179840, C[27]=116461439672085416832, C[26]=78823085262292775712. claims.reason: Exact integer replay shows the perturbation component fails at a guarded rank even though the complete deletion polynomial passes all guarded ranks in this profile. The negative component margin is not an eligible-rank or full-comparison counterexample.

limitations: The universal individual and weighted shifted comparisons remain unproved; no guarded counterexample was found.
